Failing to compute the correct coordinates in the vertex shader will result in incorrect footprint sampling [S1, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly states that when using Point Sprites, 'the correct texture coordinates must be computed in a vertex shader' because the extension computes them automatically otherwise. It further explains that these coordinates are used to 'determine the coordinates of the sub-texture containing the corresponding footprint.' Therefore, failing to compute these correct coordinates would lead to incorrect sampling of the footprint texture.

It distinguishes itself from prior ISSB implementations by computing and storing distinct kernel footprints for each voxel across all intersecting slabs, rather than storing a single footprint modulated by a slab coefficient [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that the method distinguishes itself by computing and storing distinct kernel footprints for each voxel across intersecting slabs, rather than storing a single footprint modulated by a slab coefficient. The evidence in Source [S1] explicitly states: 'Voxels have a different kernel footprint in the different slabs that they intersect. Neophytou and Mueller [14] propose to store only one footprint and to modulate it with an appropriate slab coefficient. Alternatively... we propose to compute all the different kernel footprints and to store them all in one 2D texture.' This directly supports every part of the claim.

It determines the range of buckets that must be processed for each slab [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that the kernel radius determines the range of buckets to be processed for each slab. Source [S1] explicitly confirms this in two places: 1) In the notes, it states 'Kernel Radius: The radius of the voxel's kernel determines the range of buckets (bucket_{i-radius} to bucket_{i+radius}) that must be processed for each slab.' 2) In section 3.6 Rendering, it states 'In order to render slabi, we splat all the voxels of the buckets that may intersect it: from bucket bucketi−radius to bucketi+radius, being radius the radius of the voxel's kernel.' Both sources directly support the claim.
